title: A Reduction Theorem for Clifford–Mandelbrot Sets with Real Exponent
content: Let V be an n-dimensional real inner product space, \( \vec{n}\in V \) a unit vector and p > 1 a real exponent. We study the Clifford--Mandelbrot set \( M_{p,\vec{n}} \), formed by the parameters \( \vec{c}\in V \) for which the orbit of the origin under \( \vec{x}\mapsto \) (\( \vec{x} \) ⋄ \( \vec{n} \))p ⋄ \( \vec{n} \) + \( \vec{c} \) is defined and bounded, where ⋄ is the geometric product. We prove that every such orbit stays in the plane spanned by \( \vec{n} \) and \( \vec{c} \), and that on this plane the map coincides with the principal branch of \( z\mapsto z^{p} \). Consequently, \( M_{p,\vec{n}} \) is the solid of revolution of the planar principal multibrot set about the \( \vec{n} \)-axis, so the construction does not produce genuinely higher-dimensional dynamics. The cause is structural: every map obtained by applying a function to \( \vec{x} \) ⋄ \( \vec{n} \) and multiplying by \( \vec{n} \) behaves in the same way. From the reduction we derive the identity \( \lVert F_{p}(\vec{x})\rVert=\lVert\vec{x}\rVert^{p} \), the escape radius $2^{1/(p-1)}$ (attained for even integers $p$), the exact intersection of \( M_{p,\vec{n}} \) with the \( \vec{n} \)-axis, an inner ball of radius $\kappa_{p}=(1-1/p)\,p^{-1/(p-1)}$, the limiting behaviour as $p\to1^{+}$ and \( p\to\infty \), the Hausdorff dimension of the boundary, and the discontinuity of the map across its branch locus. All statements are checked numerically.
